name: Eastern Redbud

facts.how: Flowers raw in salads; young pods cooked

caution: Eat the flowers and only the tender young pods; skip old pods and seeds. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: In March the bare branches erupt in magenta-pink flowers right off the wood. Unmistakable and cheerful.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The tangy-sweet flowers brighten a salad or top a cake; young pods can be sautéed like snow peas.
